'''Jean-Michel Savéant''' (19 September 1933  &ndash; 16 August 2020) was a French [[chemist]] who specialized in [[electrochemistry]]. He was elected member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2000 and foreign associate of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2001. He published in excess of 400 peer-reviewed articles in chemistry literature.

==Biography==
Born in [[Rennes]], Jean-Michel Savéant graduated in 1958 and obtained his PhD in 1966 at the [[École normale supérieure (rue d'Ulm)|École normale supérieure]]. In 1971 he moved to [[Paris Diderot University]] where he founded the Laboratoire d'Électrochimie Moléculaire. He was  an [[emeritus]] professor of [[electrochemistry]] in this university as well as an emeritus [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] Research Director. He was the author of over 500 [[Scientific literature|publications]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Costentin|first1=Cyrille|last2=Limoges|first2=Benoît|last3=Robert|first3=Marc|last4=Tard|first4=Cédric|date=2021-02-26|title=A Pioneering Career in Electrochemistry: Jean-Michel Savéant|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-03224397/file/JMS%20Career-MS.pdf|journal=ACS Catalysis|volume=11 |issue=6 |language=en|pages=3224–3238|doi=10.1021/acscatal.0c05632|s2cid=233960570 |issn=2155-5435}}</ref>

==Major contributions==
Jean-Michel Savéant's scientific activity is outlined by the foundation and development of a new discipline - molecular [[electrochemistry]]. Molecular electrochemistry has transferred the knowledge acquired by electrochemistry towards various fields of chemistry and biochemistry, in particular towards the chemistry of [[Electron transfer|electron]] and proton transfer, [[Radical (chemistry)|free radical chemistry]], [[Reactivity (chemistry)|chemical reactivity]] theory, [[coordination chemistry]], [[photochemistry]], solid [[Physical chemistry|physico-chemistry]], [[enzymology]] and [[Catalysis|catalytic]] activation of small molecules, especially those involved in solving contemporary energy challenges.
